title: A magnetic-field insensitive gate set for trapped-ion nuclear spin qubits
authors: Jonathan Paul Home, Jeremy Flannery, Matteo Mazzanti, Jan Apolin, Shreyans Jain
abstract: We outline a complete set of operations for manipulating nuclear spin qubits of trapped-ions stored in high magnetic fields such as required for Penning trapping, where the nuclear and electron spins are largely decoupled due to the dominance of the external field Hamiltonian. The reduced nuclear magnetic moment results in insensitivity to external magnetic fields compared to the use of an electron spin, but also makes the nuclear spin hard to manipulate on fast timescales. To maintain speed, we propose a two-qubit phase gate technique which utilizes the electron spin, but for which the qubit remains protected from magnetic fields through retaining the nuclear encoding. This method works for magnetic-field insensitive qubits at lower fields as well as for both microwave and laser field gradients.
summary: This paper details a method to implement fast, high-fidelity two-qubit gates for nuclear spin qubits in trapped ions. By utilizing a four-tone microwave drive, the authors overcome the inherent slowness of nuclear spin manipulation while ensuring the gate operation remains robust against external magnetic field fluctuations. This advances the feasibility of using nuclear spins for quantum computation.
main_problem: Developing a complete set of fast, magnetic-field insensitive quantum gates for nuclear spin qubits in trapped ions, especially in high magnetic field regimes.
main_result: The authors propose a four-tone microwave gate scheme that achieves gate speeds comparable to electron spin gates while maintaining insensitivity to external magnetic field noise.
method: The technique involves using a multi-tone microwave drive, carefully detuned from resonance, to induce conditional phase shifts between nuclear spin states rather than relying on slow, direct nuclear spin flips.
model_or_system: The system is trapped ions (e.g., Be+, Ca+) where the qubit is encoded in the nuclear spin, coupled to the electron spin via the hyperfine interaction. The Hamiltonian includes terms for the hyperfine interaction and the external magnetic field.
key_observables: Gate fidelity, gate speed (compared to electron spin flips), and susceptibility to external magnetic field noise.
important_parameters: High magnetic fields (e.g., 3 T, 6 T), hyperfine coupling constant (A), and the relative phases of the applied microwave tones.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the magnetic field is along the z-axis and that the four-tone drive can effectively decouple the gate operation from magnetic field noise.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the energy level splittings and the schematic implementation of the two-qubit gate schemes, comparing two-tone and four-tone drive mechanisms.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the physical challenge (speed vs. field sensitivity) to deriving the Hamiltonian for the gate, proposing the four-tone drive as the solution, and analyzing its noise robustness compared to single-drive methods.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the critical challenge of scaling quantum computation in trapped ions by providing a pathway to fast, robust gates for nuclear spins, which are otherwise difficult to control.
